title: Molson Coors ditches its TV-era workflow to move at creator speed, quadrupling engagement
tldr: A concrete case study of a big brand overhauling its content operations to move at creator speed, with measurable engagement gains. Real numbers plus workflow change make it useful ammunition for content ops arguments.
angle: What legacy brands must dismantle in their content workflows to actually operate at creator speed.

title: 9/11 and "never forget" collide with the meme generation's dark humor
tldr: Explores how a generation with no firsthand memory of an event consumes and reinterprets it through algorithm-rewarded dark humor. A sharp lens on media-consumption habits and emotional distance shaping content.
angle: How generational memory gaps reshape which stories brands and institutions can tell — and how.

title: How the creator economy rewired brand strategy
tldr: A macro look at how creators have restructured the way brands approach strategy, not just tactics. Useful framing for anyone tracking the shift from campaigns to always-on creator partnerships.
angle: From campaign calendar to creator operating system: what actually changed in brand strategy.

title: Whistles marks 50 years by casting 50 customers found through mysterious fly-posters across London
tldr: A fashion brand swapped models for 50 real customers aged 19-72, found via guerrilla posters and shot in a day. A strong example of human-centered, people-over-polish content and casting as campaign.
angle: Casting real customers over models: when authenticity becomes the whole creative idea.

title: I Tracked 13,184 AI Citations Across 4 LLMs: Here's What I Learned
tldr: Original research on what sources LLMs cite across four models — practical data for anyone optimizing content for AI answer engines. Fresh empirical grounding in a hyped area.
angle: What 13k AI citations reveal about which content LLMs actually trust — and how to earn them.

title: Consumers don't experience channels
tldr: Argues brands obsess over channels while consumers experience only the brand, challenging omnichannel orthodoxy. A useful provocation for content architecture and planning.
angle: Stop planning by channel: designing content around the single brand experience consumers actually have.

title: Chipotle is 'gatekeeping nothing' in latest 100 Creators campaign
tldr: Chipotle enlists 100 creators in an openness-themed campaign, a scaled creator-collaboration model worth breaking down. Concrete example of creator-led brand content at volume.
angle: What 100-creator campaigns teach us about managing content at volume without losing coherence.

title: 'The problem is the execution': The role of comms in the data center controversy
tldr: How communications teams can defuse reputational blowback around data centers by surfacing community concerns early. A timely issue-management and stakeholder-engagement case.
angle: Getting ahead of community backlash: comms lessons from the data-center building boom.

title: AI is putting marketing's in-house model to the test
tldr: Examines how AI is reshaping the build-vs-outsource decision for in-house marketing and content teams. Relevant to editorial ops and content governance choices.
why_fresh: AI's structural impact on team models
angle: Does AI make in-house content teams stronger or hollow them out?

title: What's in and out for creators heading into Q4
tldr: A forward-looking read on which creator formats and tactics are rising or fading into Q4. Useful trend-spotting for content planning.
angle: The Q4 creator shortlist: what to double down on and what to retire.

title: Andrew Tindall: Humans can't spot AI ads. Can AI rate human ones?
tldr: Provocative piece on humans failing to distinguish AI-made ads and whether AI can judge creative quality. Cuts to the heart of synthetic media and human-vs-machine craft debates.
angle: If audiences can't tell AI ads apart, what's left of the case for human craft?

title: "Many have said it couldn't be done": Local news site Lookout Santa Cruz is profitable thanks to ads and memberships
tldr: A rare profitable local-news case built on ads plus memberships, six years in. Concrete business-model evidence for sustainable owned media.
angle: What a profitable local newsroom teaches brands about membership-driven owned media.

title: Openness to paid social media features varies by how Britons use social media
tldr: YouGov data linking willingness to pay for social features to how people actually use platforms. Useful audience-insight data on media-consumption segmentation.
angle: Usage style predicts willingness to pay: segmenting audiences by how, not just what, they consume.

title: Universal Music is launching an AI music platform with ElevenLabs
tldr: UMG is building a licensed AI platform for remixes and mashups from its catalog via ElevenLabs. A landmark in rights-holders embracing rather than fighting generative media.
angle: When rights-holders build the AI tools: what UMG x ElevenLabs signals for content licensing.
